complexity.notes: Each extension costs O(window) because the slice plus `in` scan rechecks the whole window, which stays linear only because printable ASCII bounds any duplicate-free window to 95 characters; on an unbounded alphabet this would be quadratic, where ||a sliding window storing each character's last-seen index|| stays O(n). The `if length:` guard has the same effect as the previous version's membership-based decrement but reads more directly.
complexity.summary: Sliding window that advances the left edge one position per iteration, shrinks the window by one, then re-extends it while the next character is not already in s[i:i+length]; tracks the maximum window length and breaks early once the remaining text cannot beat it.
